results.title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.1.1: Keyboard | WAI | W3C
results.content: Understanding SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) In Brief Goal Everything can be done with a keyboard except freehand movements. What to do Ensure pointer actions have a keyboard equivalent. Why it's important Many people rely on the keyboard interface, including blind and some mobility impaired people. Success Criterion (SC)

results.title: Understanding Guideline 2.1: Keyboard Accessible | WAI | W3C
results.content: Intent If all functionality can be achieved using the keyboard, it can be accomplished by keyboard users, by speech input (which creates keyboard input), by mouse (using on-screen keyboards), and by a wide variety of assistive technologies that create simulated keystrokes as their output.

results.title: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible — Keyboard Focus Indicators
results.content: The definitive guide to WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible: why every interactive element needs a visible focus indicator, how to use :focus-visible, never remove the outline, contrast expectations, copy-ready CSS, and testing.

results.title: Focus Management: The Complete Accessibility Guide
results.content: Focus Management: The Complete Accessibility Guide Focus is the keyboard user's cursor. This guide covers every part of managing it well — tabindex, :focus-visible, moving focus programmatically, focus traps, restoration, roving tabindex, skip links, and route-change focus — with copy-ready code mapped to WCAG 2.2.

results.title: [Draft] Focus user-controlled - WCAG 3 Support Material | WAI | W3C
results.content: The keyboard focus automatically moves to the next interactive elements in keyboard navigation order on completion of some user action, such when the focus moves between the fields for a time-based one-time password (TOTP) code.
